name: Euler's theorem and the totient
formula: \gcd(a, n) = 1 \implies a^{\varphi(n)} \equiv 1 \pmod n, \qquad \varphi(n) = n \prod_{\text{prime } p \mid n} \left(1 - \frac{1}{p}\right)
whenToUse: Remainders of huge powers modulo a composite number, such as the last two digits of a power. Also counting the integers up to $n$ that share no factor with $n$.
example: Last two digits of $3^{2023}$: $\varphi(100) = 40$ and $2023 = 40 \cdot 50 + 23$, so we need $3^{23}$. Since $3^{10} = 59049 \equiv 49$ and $3^{20} \equiv 49^2 = 2401 \equiv 1$, the answer is $3^{23} \equiv 27$.
pitfall: The base must be coprime to $n$. And $\varphi(n)$ is a period, not always the smallest one: here $3^{20} \equiv 1$ already, so a shorter cycle may exist.
